### Architect · Answer

Event: `6b3cd4806df74ef9b1ca471d297dafe1` · 2026-10-06T01:29:25Z

> Ruled; the brief has a dated section with the full text, owned paths and page lines (.wash/local/SMP1-implementer.md, "rulings from the early checkpoint").
> 
> Q1: (a). Queue::reconcile (libs/stride lib.rs:289) exempts one running budget from leaving on `lost`; with several harts, a budget running on hart B whose only thread is the running one would be dequeued by hart A's reconcile and never picked again until a wake. That R12 hole cannot be closed by swapping cur/pending at the lock, so (b) is refused. Shape: Queue::reconcile takes the running set (a predicate over the per-hart runners' curs); Queue::pick takes the exclusion predicate rule 6 names (SMP3 replaces it); Cpu stays the one-hart wrapper so the model and the_crate_and_the_model_agree stand unchanged; a Harts<B,N,H> of Runner{cur,pending} per boot index carries accrue/bill/settle/switch/destroy per hart. Stride unit tests for the set, the exclusion, per-runner pending and MIN_CHARGE. The model gains no running set in SMP1: SMP2 owns R12 across harts and gets per-hart current, set reconcile, exclusion pick and an H-hart differential; a follow-up line in the report. libs/stride joins the owned paths, the differential unchanged as the condition.
> 
> Q2: allowed, into the per-hart block: the running thread's context address (header slot 1), the hart's current PID/TID (current_pid reads the running hart's), and the hart's own saved context for the kernel's thread (PID 1's no_thread). Slot 1, the scratch word and no_thread go; the block is kernel data mapped in every address space, reached by sscratch. Exact replacement sentences for memory-layout.md (both "Per-process kernel data" paragraphs, the satp paragraph) are in the brief; the satp status keeps "one hart is argued from the code" until SMP2. Those paragraphs join the owned paths; scheduling.md's queue line gains "A reconcile keeps a budget queued while any hart runs it."
> 
> Q3: per-case `smp = [2]` is step 1's form; `--smp N` touches B7's main.rs: ask B7 first.

Event: `eaa614f9510662717abb05cc02e839cd` · 2026-10-06T01:35:13Z

> SMP1 Q4 (blocking for the secondary harts' start; I'm building the rest meanwhile). Each started hart needs its own kernel stack (kmain) and trap stack; the boot hart's are the loader's KERNEL_STACK_TOP and TRAP_STACK_TOP, 8 pages each, guarded by unmapped neighbours (the trap handler's 'ran out of kernel stack' check relies on a fault). Up to 7 more harts x 16 pages. Not settled by the brief or memory-layout.md. Options:
> (a) RECOMMENDED: a new kernel-area window HART_STACKS at the kernel area's empty low part, 0xffc0_0000 (Sv32, root 1023, free below KERNEL_TEXT 0xffd0_0000, 1 MiB) and 0xffff_ffff_ffc0_0000 (Sv39, same offset, free above the DMA window): per secondary boot index i, a kernel stack and a trap stack of 8 pages each, each with an unmapped guard page below, 7 x 18 pages = 504 KiB. Frames taken from the memory manager page by page (no run needed), mapped as global kernel pages when the hart is started (only harts started cost RAM). Adds constants to libs/layout and a row to memory-layout.md's two address maps (Sv32 1023 row, Sv39 kernel-area table).
> (b) static .bss arrays (as the spike): 448 KiB of .bss for MAX_HARTS-1 whether or not the harts exist, no guards, and the 1 MiB kernel data region gets tight.
> (c) frames through the physmap: no layout change, but no guard pages, so an overflow writes a neighbouring frame silently.
> Owned paths for (a): libs/layout/src/lib.rs (the constants and their asserts) and memory-layout.md's address-map rows.
> Progress: libs/stride done per the ruling (Queue reconcile/pick predicates, Runner, Harts<B,N,H>, Cpu as the 1-hart wrapper over the same wiring, marks' running predicate, 3 unit tests); host run in progress.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `3b4ae711fa25ffdab54c61bff208efa8` · 2026-10-06T01:43:17Z

> Q4: (a), the HART_STACKS window with guard pages, for the reason you give: irq.rs:136's "ran out of kernel stack" is a fault-based check, and a stack with no unmapped page below it loses it; (b) and (c) are refused.
> 
> Shape, in libs/layout beside KERNEL_STACK_TOP/TRAP_STACK_TOP (both widths): a HART_STACKS window of MAX_HARTS slots, each slot = 1 guard page + KERNEL_STACK_PAGES (8) + 1 guard + TRAP_STACK_PAGES (8) = 18 pages, so the window is MAX_HARTS x 18 pages (8 x 72 KiB = 576 KiB), with compile-time asserts: the window is inside the kernel area, clear of the image, the PLIC and DMA register windows and the process area, and on Sv32 fits under 1 MiB (the hardware-bounds table gains the row: `HART_STACKS` | kernel area, Sv32 1 MiB | MAX_HARTS x 18 pages <= window | compile (layout) | memory-layout.md "The two address maps"). Only a started hart's slot is backed; the guards are never mapped.
> 
> One definition, not two: the boot hart's stacks are slot 0 of the window, and KERNEL_STACK_TOP / TRAP_STACK_TOP are defined as slot 0's tops (the loader keeps mapping what those constants name, so the loader does not change and the boot hart never switches stacks; the kernel maps slots 1..n when it starts harts). The two address maps gain one row each for the window (replacing the two separate stack rows with "hart stacks: MAX_HARTS slots of kernel and trap stack with guard pages, slot 0 the boot hart's"), and memory-layout.md's row 374 (G bit on the stacks) stays true. Add to SMP1's page lines; owned paths gain libs/layout for these constants and their asserts.
